collect.comment: One run per page. Three runs (a median, to smooth runner noise) tripled the slowest step in the deploy for a gate that is already generous.

assertMatrix.comment: The portfolio itself. The category scores are the real gate — they are normalised, so they mean the same thing on a laptop and on a shared CI runner. CLS is a layout property and barely varies with hardware, so it stays exact. Performance is gated at 0.85, below the 0.90 the site is built to: the same build that scores 0.95 to 0.97 on a laptop has come back at 0.87 from a shared runner, and at one run per page a gate set at the target fails on that noise alone. A real regression still has ten points to fall through before it gets here.

The editor, the print CV and the 404 page. None is on a visitor's path to the portfolio, so accessibility gates the build and speed does not. 404.html sits here despite being the lightest page in the repo — inline CSS, no scripts, no requests — precisely because there is nothing for a performance budget to protect, while its size makes the score the noisiest to measure: at one run per page a few hundred milliseconds of runner jitter is the difference between 0.8 and 1.0.
